To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimal action policy balances exploration and control; (2) the optimal world model summarizes the causal structure of the process at different levels of detail; (3) the optimal world models and action policies are obtained from a single objective function that balances prediction and complexity.

(1) the optimal model is an abstraction of the process in the presence of action; (2) the optimal policy balances exploration and control; and (3) the optimal model summarizes, at different levels, the process's structure in the presence of actions.

the optimal model and action policy are derived by maximizing the mutual information between the learner's observations and the process's causal structure, while minimizing the mutual information between model parameters and observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a quantitative approach to interactive behavior and learning.
a quantitative approach to adaptive behavior, which is based on a principle that integrates model- and decision making.
the principles of optimal interactive learning and the resulting optimal models of the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a new approach to interactive learning that integrates model- and decision making into one theoretical framework.

the proposed principle of optimal interactive learning is able to derive optimal action policies, optimal world models, and optimal levels of abstraction, which are consistent with each other, in a unified manner.

the proposed framework provides a unifying principle for the integration of model- and decision making, and for the emergence of explorative behavior in the absence of randomness in the action policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a general framework for the analysis of learning in the presence of a learner, and that we derive the fundamental consequences of such a framework for learning and behavior.
the proposed approach is a generalization of the principle of maximum likelihood, where the latter only considers passive observation, and the former also considers active interaction with the world.
it is possible to integrate model-based and model-free reinforcement learning into one coherent theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the principle of maximizing prediction power while minimizing complexity leads to an information-theoretic foundation for interactive learning and adaptive control, which is applicable to both model- and decision-based approaches to learning.

the principle of maximizing predictive power in the face of feedback is an alternative to the principle of minimizing surprise, and that it leads to a more general and mathematically tractable theory of interactive learning.
feedback is an essential element for understanding learning, as it is for understanding the behavior of complex adaptive systems.
